Signed from Union Saint-Gilloise on 15 August 2026 for EUR 24.5m on a five-year deal, a club-record fee for an Israeli player, after an Inter Milan move collapsed. Right-sided player brought in as competition on the right flank. He post-dates Solio's data entirely and is still absent from the FPL bootstrap as of today, so Solio has him at zero. Held to 1250 rather than a starter's load because the deal is subject to international clearance, he arrived six days before the opener, and he is 21 and new to England. NOTE: code is 0 because he has no FPL element yet.

Solio projects roughly 31 full matches for a player signed on a free on 7 August after a trial in the Como Cup. His entire recent workload is eight Ajax appearances plus three World Cup games; he had not played between October 2024 and February 2026 because of a knee injury, and the reporting states Palace wanted to be sure about his fitness before signing. In the final friendly at Freiburg he did not start, coming on to replace Chadi Riad. Both the availability risk and the current pecking order point well below 2822.

Solio's 445 is a stale artefact: his club_2526 is still listed as EVE and the number looks like a part-season remnant. He joined Palace on 11 August in a straight swap for Brennan Johnson, both sides valued at around EUR 25.8m, and started the Freiburg friendly on 15 August for his first Palace minutes. A club does not trade away its first-choice right winger for a player who then plays five matches' worth of football.

Solio has the club-record signing at roughly a quarter of a season. He cost a fixed GBP 43m plus GBP 5m in add-ons in January on a four-and-a-half-year deal, and he started the final pre-season friendly at centre-forward while Mateta, back from the World Cup, did not. Palace-focused analysis in July described him as the long-term number nine whose vertical, box-presence profile fits Sage's system. Set at 1950 rather than a full starter's load because the striker slot is genuinely shared three ways.

The other side of the striker split. Sage's system uses one number nine and Palace hold three Premier League strikers; Mateta did not start the final friendly. His exit situation is unresolved: a January move to AC Milan collapsed on medical grounds, Juventus interest was reported through May and June at a EUR 20-30m valuation, and reporting says his contract is running down with Palace preferring not to sell cheaply. The window is open until 1 September. Not zeroed, because he is registered, fit and available today.

Solio projects a 962-minute jump on his 2173 last season, and that projection predates three August arrivals who all land in the wide and attacking areas: McNeil on 11 August, Guessand on 12 August and Khalaili on 15 August. Palace also play in the Europa League league phase this season, which forces domestic rotation. Proposed figure still sits slightly above his 2025/26 total.

Same cause as Sarr. Three wide or attacking players arrived after Solio's data cut-off and Pino did not appear in the XI or the substitutions listed for the final friendly at Freiburg. He is the most directly displaced by McNeil arriving on the left.

He also scored in the Como Cup friendly against Al-Ula.

A full-season deal with a purchase obligation implies a larger role than the half-season Solio's number is scaled from. He came off the bench for Strand Larsen at Freiburg.

Still the first-choice right wing-back, but Palace added two players who can fill that slot after Solio's cut-off: Mingueza on 9 July and Khalaili on 15 August, the latter explicitly as competition on the right. Combined with the Europa League league phase, 34 full matches is too high a ceiling.

Second, he missed the July Swindon friendly with a knock and has never exceeded 2552 Premier League minutes in a season, so Solio's 3158 is above his established ceiling in a year with Europa League football.

Rotation midfielder who came off the bench for Wharton at Freiburg. Cheick Doucoure is back in training and played in pre-season after roughly 18 months out, which restores a competitor Solio's numbers do not account for, and Lerma and Devenny remain. Trimmed to help fund the attacking arrivals.

Small uplift. He scored twice against Swindon in July, scored again in the Como Cup against Al-Ula, and came on for Sarr at Freiburg, so he is fit and being used. Kept low because he is third in a three-way striker queue and is a candidate to be moved on before 1 September.

reinforcement_risk.note: Maxence Lacroix left for Chelsea on 30 July for GBP 52m and the Guardian preview says the defence still needs a natural leader to replace him, with budget constraints limiting spending. Tomiyasu was a free-transfer trialist and Riad is a year removed from an ACL injury. If Palace sign a centre-back before 1 September, both proposed figures fall.

Palace hold three Premier League strikers for one slot in Sage's system and reporting says at least one is expected to be offloaded. Mateta is the most likely to move, with a collapsed Milan deal and repeated Juventus interest behind him. A Mateta sale would push Strand Larsen and Nketiah up sharply; a Strand Larsen sale would do the reverse.

Chelsea held face-to-face talks with Palace on 12 August and Man Utd are also reported as interested, with Palace publicly standing firm and asking around EUR 100m. Palace's stated stance is that Sage wants buyers not sellers, and Wharton is contracted to 2029, so a sale is not the base case, but it is unresolved with the window open to 1 September. If he leaves, Lerma, Hughes, Doucoure and Devenny absorb the minutes.

Palace have already spent EUR 24.5m here on 15 August after adding McNeil and Guessand in the preceding four days. Further additions in this area look unlikely, but the reverse risk is real: this group is now overstocked and one of Pino, Guessand or Esse could leave before deadline day.

injuries.issue: As of 2026-08-16 the FPL bootstrap flags no Crystal Palace player as injured or doubtful. The only two 'u' statuses are Uche (returned to Getafe) and Cardines (loaned to Bristol City), both squad departures rather than injuries. Adam Wharton carries chance_of_playing 100 dated 2026-07-23, i.e. a knock already resolved.

Long-term knee/Achilles absence. His last competitive appearance for Palace was January 2025 and he was out for roughly 18 months. Not currently flagged in FPL and he played in pre-season, but he is building back rather than match-fit.

unknowns: Anan Khalaili has no FPL element and therefore no code; his delta is filed with code 0. If the balancing script joins on code it will drop his 1250 minutes and the total will read 36367 rather than 37617. Flagging explicitly rather than hiding the problem by omitting him.

Khalaili's FPL position is unknown. Transfermarkt lists him as right midfield, the wire copy says he primarily plays on the right, and one outlet described him as a wing-back signed to compete with Munoz. He could be classified DEF or MID when FPL adds him, which changes which pool his minutes come out of.

The striker split between Strand Larsen, Mateta and Nketiah is the single largest source of error in this allocation. The evidence for Strand Larsen leading is real but circumstantial: a club-record fee, one pre-season start, and a system that fits him. Mateta started the 2025/26 Conference League final and scored the winner. If Mateta stays and wins the slot, my Strand Larsen and Mateta figures should be swapped.

I could not obtain a beat-reporter or podcast source stating an expected opening-day XI. The two aggregator sites found (Sports Mole predicted XI, starting11.com) were both stale, still listing Brennan Johnson and Rio Cardines, who left on 11 August, and starting11 was based on five fan submissions in a 4-4-2 that contradicts the confirmed back three. Both were discarded rather than used.

The 15 August Freiburg lineup is distorted by the summer World Cup. Munoz, Sarr, Richards, Kamada, Mateta, Henderson and Tomiyasu all had extended international breaks, so pre-season starts understate the internationals and overstate the squad players. I have weighted it accordingly but the distortion cannot be fully removed.

The lastwordonsports article describing Khalaili as competition for Munoz rather than his replacement returned HTTP 403 and could not be verified directly. That framing came from a search-result summary only, so I have relied on the FOX/AP wire copy for the underlying facts and treated the role description as unconfirmed.

Whether Palace still sign a centre-back before 1 September. The Guardian preview identifies it as the outstanding need and Raphael Le Guen of Brest was reported as agreeing personal terms, but I found no confirmation the deal completed and he does not appear in the Wikipedia transfer ledger.

Chris Richards, Jaydee Canvot, Will Hughes and Adam Wharton were trimmed on a general Europa-League-rotation argument rather than player-specific reporting. These four are the weakest-evidenced deltas in the set and are marked low confidence for that reason.
